classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the vertex and positive time intercept of a projectile-height model, using symmetry and contextual rejection of the initial root.

content.prompt: The height, $h$ metres, reached by a ball after $t$ seconds when thrown vertically upwards is given by $h=25t-4.9t^2$. Find, correct to three decimal places, the maximum height reached and the time the ball is in the air.

answer.short:
Maximum height: $31.888\text{ m}$. Time in the air: $5.102\text{ s}$.

The maximum occurs halfway between the two time intercepts.
answer.worked:
The ball is at ground level when $h=0$.
$$\begin{align*}t(25-4.9t)&=0\\t&=0\quad\text{or}\quad\frac{250}{49}.\end{align*}$$
The root $t=0$ is the launch time, so the time in the air is $\dfrac{250}{49}\text{ s}\approx5.102\text{ s}$.

The height graph is a downward-opening parabola. By symmetry, its maximum occurs halfway between its time intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}t_{\max}&=\frac{0+\frac{250}{49}}{2}\\t_{\max}&=\frac{125}{49}.\end{align*}$$
Substituting this time gives
$$\begin{align*}h_{\max}&=25\left(\frac{125}{49}\right)-\frac{49}{10}\left(\frac{125}{49}\right)^2\\h_{\max}&=\frac{3125}{98}\\h_{\max}&\approx31.888\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
